summary: The neutral stance (as relayed in the Portfolio Manager's 10-21 decision; I did not re-read my own output file) held up as a sizing call. SPY stayed above its 200-day (722.77, 6.4% above) and the tape was mildly positive: SPY's cumulative return moved from +0.335% to +0.862%, about +0.5% on the day, so a risk-on lean would have been marginally better but neutral did no harm. The defensive and favored-sector names the book holds lagged on the day: DPZ -1.6%, IDXX -0.8%, WMT -0.2%. The Technology avoid call was supported by CARG (-1.5%, the one tech name bought). BTC was +1.9% on the day. One day is too short to grade anything; the stance stays pending.
update: No change to the stance. Two soft spots to watch: (1) the favor tilt toward Staples and Health Care did not pay on 10-21 (all three held names down while SPY rose), so do not lean harder on defensives unless 21-day leadership (XLP +7.1%, XLV +6.4%) persists. (2) The 5-day tech slide (XLK -5.5%, QQQ -3.5%) is the main risk to a neutral read; a sharp rebound would argue for upgrading toward risk-on, while SPY nearing 722.77 or HYG weakening past its 200-day (currently -1.4% below) would argue for risk-off. L1 (stop anchoring) applies to Proposer and Portfolio Manager, not to this role, and did not shape the call.
